sentences.text: For that purpose, notices were issued by the Respondent under Section 19-B of the Maharashtra Highways Act, 1955.
3. The Petitioners claim co-owners of the area stated to be acquired.
There are divisions out of Gat No. 45 which are being acquired.
It is their case that the Petitioners are ready for acquisition by way of agreement.
If a party prepared for acquisition by way of agreement, it is entitled to additional compensation.

According to the Petitioners, instead of issuing a notice under Section 19-B specifying the large area of Gat No.45, a specific notice should have been issued regarding the land in the Petitioners' possession.
Since it is not done, the Petitioners' right to additional compensation under Section 19-B is being prejudiced even though they are ready by acquisition by way of agreement.
4. It appears that there is a family dispute.
Respondent Nos. 5 & 6, also developers, are brothers of Petitioner No. 3, who are contesting the Petitioners' claim regarding the extent of share in the said land.
5. In the aforesaid fact, it is noted that on 26 September 2023, while adjourning the petitions, the Division Bench of this Court granted ad-interim order.
Respondent authorities make a grievance that as as a consequence of the interim further steps of acquisition Sneha Chavan 3 34-WP-11920-2023.docx are stalled.
The learned counsel for the Respondent/Corporation states that the land is required for the Pune (East) Ring-road.
He submits that in view of the ad-interim order, neither acquisition by negotiation is going forward nor can compulsory acquisition be undertaken.
6. Since acquisition through compulsory mode is a lengthy procedure, the legislature has introduced acquisition by way of negotiations and additional compensation by way of incentive.
The purpose and object behind introducing Section 19-B will have to be understood in its proper perspective.
The Acquiring Authority is not expected to decide complicated the inter se civil disputes at the stage of entering into negotiation.

Section 19-B would come in play when a person competent to consent enters into the agreement with the acquiring authority to get additional compensation in furtherance of the object of speedy acquisition.

7. In the present, case, because of this litigation, neither the acquisition by way of agreement is taking place, nor compulsory acquisition is proceeding ahead, directly affecting the public interest.
Such a position will defeat the legislative intent behind section 19-B of the Act.

Learned counsel for the Respondent/Acquiring Body has drawn our attention to Section 19-C (1) and (2), which postulates that the amount determined needs to be deposited with the Land Acquisition Officer for payment to interested persons.
Sneha Chavan 4 34-WP-11920-2023.docx 8.
Ultimately, the interest of both the Petitioners and private Respondents is now only in monetary terms.
As long as their monetary interest is safeguarded, we do not find any reason to restrain the Authority from proceeding further.

sentences.text:
Therefore, according to us, the appropriate course of action would be to direct the Respondents /State and Authorities to deposit the amount as per Section 19-C(1) and (2) inclusive of 25%
incentive and after the amount is deposited, further steps as contemplated under Section 19-C(4)
can be taken.

However, since we will be vacating the ad-interim order, we do not intend to dispose of the Writ Petition at this stage, but we will defer the hearing to ensure that the amount is deposited before the next date.
The amount be deposited in the Registry of this Court subject to further orders that will be passed, i.e. directions under section 19-C(4), by 12 June 2024.
10. The ad-interim order granted earlier is vacated, in light of the directions to deposit the amount.
11. We are of the opinion that considering the near relation of the Petitioners and private Respondents, the issue needs to be resolved amicably between them, which is beneficial to all the parties.
If such agreement takes place, the said fact be intimated to the Respondent/State and Municipal Corporation.
Sneha Chavan 5 34-WP-11920-2023.docx 12.
Stand over to 12 June 2024.
